findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: Person in charge of food service had to leave early to pick up a sick child. Owner thought that she was food manager certified but the certificate on the wall reads food handler. Inspector was able to speak with the food employee on phone and was able to ask questions. The facility is currently running like a low risk facility as the food employee had to leave. No food preparation or service will take place by other employees. The owner was contacted and stated that they want the food handler employee to become manager certified. CFPM class information was provided to the facility at the time of inspection.

(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Hand towels were missing at the hand sink when inspector washed their hands. Towels were provided. The violation was corrected on site. Maintain hand towel holder stocked with single use/disposable towels. (Paper towels)

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: Inspector observed a box of Little Debbie shack cakes along with some other foods in boxes stored on the floor under the pizza prep table. Store food a minimum of 6 inches above the floor. 

(A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Frost and ice are observed to be accumulated on the sides of the glass top freezers. Defrost the freezers and maintain them clean. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed tile in the back area by the mop and 3 part sinks to be broken and missing. This is allowing raw wood floor to be exposed to water and soil. Repair the floor covering so that it is smooth and cleanable. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

This morning the CFPM was ill and could not come into work. Please ensure that there are enough certified food protection managers to cover in situations such as this. This was discussed last year during the inspection. Manager Kathy and employee Candace both expressed the desire to do the certification. Inspector strongly suggests having 3 or more managers to cover all shifts and needed time off.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 

Pizza is holding in the display case at 116F. The pizza was cooked at 10:30 am. The pizza will be used or discarded at 2:30 pm. The keeping of a time as a control log was discussed with manager and this will begin today. Time as a control form was filled out with facility at time of inspeciton.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

The facility has cardboard on the shelves of the walk in cooler under food items. The cardboard shall be removed and replaced (if necessary) with a material that is smooth cleanable and that has holes to allow air flow and proper cooling in the unit.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed hot dogs in the back refrigerator to lack date marking. Employee indicated hot dogs had been pulled 3 days ago from freezer storage. Ensure hot dogs are date marked and discarded within 7 days if not used before that 7 day date. Discussed proper date marking techniques with PIC and employees. Employee put date on the hot dogs. COS.

findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed milk crates to be directly placed on the floor of the walk-in cooler. Cease practice. Discussed keeping food 6 inches off the ground with employees and PIC.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple freezers (all chest freezer, top freezer in the back room) to have build-up of frost. Ensure routine cleaning of freezers - defrost as needed. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 3/4/20 and 6/11/21.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no quaternary ammonium test strips. Facility had run out. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 4/6/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed a new hand air dryer in the bathroom. Holes are present where previous equipment was. Ensure all holes are caulked before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed facility to be preparing hot dogs and torpedos for hot holding on rollers; however, PIC during inspection (who prepared items this morning) is only a food handler. A CFPM must be present for hot holding with rollers; otherwise, food handlers can be present during other hours of operation. Ensure CFPM’s are present for this process. Provided copy of CFPM training so facility can have more than one CFPM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed soda nozzles to have debris. Ensure soda nozzles are routinely washed, rinsed, and sanitized. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/4/20.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple chest freezers to have a build-up of frost. Ensure routine cleaning of chest freezers. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/4/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

(REPEAT) Observed mop to be stored within mop bucket. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/4/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed mop sink area to have the Nudo board covering the repairs that were necessary from previous inspections; however, caulking has not occurred in this area. Caulk around the Nudo board before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements. Facility will review documents with all employees and sign documents. Inspector will follow-up on 3/13/20.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.12  (C) Interior of microwave is heavily soiled. Interior cavity and door seals of microwaves must be cleaned and sanitized at least once every 24 hours. Reference 4-602.12.

Observed microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed routine cleaning of microwave with PIC. Microwaves should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 24 hours.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Several food contact surfaces are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed soda nozzles to have build up of debris. Discussed routine cleaning of soda nozzles with PIC - wash, rinse, sanitize. Observed pizza paddle and ice scoop to be placed directly on top of pizza and ice machines. Discussed having clean surfaces for food contact equipment such as an ice scoop storage bucket or a tray that can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized for pizza paddle. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of interior of chest freezers are no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed multiple chest freezers (see temperature list above; chest freezers #1 and 3, as well as ice freezer outside) to have large accumulations of ice. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored incorrectly in-between uses. Mops should be stored in a manner that allows to drip dry and/or air dry. Correctly hung mop during inspection. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Cartons of shell eggs noted stored above gallons of milk in the  display walk-in cooler. Packages of raw bacon noted stored on shelf directly above single customer drinks in the display walk-in cooler. Items were rearranged at the time of inspection. 

-> Please store raw animal products in a manner to protect from cross-contamination. Store raw animal products below ready to eat food items.  Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
-Hot dogs in roller unit found holding between 118F-123F. Operator indicated hot dogs were to be discarded in 30 minutes. Thermostat on unit was turned higher at the time of inspection. 
-Pizza slices on the middle tier shelf found holding between 122F-126F. Top shelf pizzas were measured 150F. Observed light bulb on the top shelf to be bigger and noticeably brighter than those on the bottom two shelves. Discussed replacing smaller bulbs. Discussed turning up the thermostat on the unit. Pizza discarded. 

-> Hot holding food items must be maintained with temperatures above 135F. Use thermometers to ensure temperatures are holding adequate. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
-Bottles of bleach, degreaser, sanitizer, floor cleaner, plant fertilizer noted stored on shelf directly above the clean drain board at the 3 compartment sink. Chemicals must be stored in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food preparation areas, and clean utensils. Chemicals moved to approved area during inspection. 
-Container of Raid domestic bug killer noted stored with water bottles sold to customers. Chemical moved. Use commercial grade pesticides, and stored to prevent contamination. 
-Large container of Spectracide Seed and Grass Killer noted stored on shelf above 3 compartment sink. Container was moved during inspection. 
-Sanitizer tabs noted stored on electric box above pizza cutting table near the pizza oven. Sanitizer relocated. 

->Toxic materials that are not required for the operation and maintenance of a food establishment must be removed. Reference 7.202.11.
->Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Tool bag noted sitting directly on cutting board table top of counter where pizza oven is stored, where pizzas are sliced. Discussed the importance of keeping this space dedicated to food and in a manner to prevent potential contamination. Bag was relocated during inspection.

->Food and non-food contact surfaces must be maintained clean and free from contamination. Reference 4-202.15.
